tasks.title: Module skeleton, README stub, own types (`StartRequest`, `Route`, `Receipt`, `AttemptStatus`, `TechnicalEvent`), error codes, `Config` limits, ports (`RouteResolver`, `BriefSource`, `AgentDriver`, `WorkspaceManager`, `EventSink`) and boundary/import/no-AI tests
tasks.objective: A new isolated package exposes frozen own types, ports and limits, and tests prove it imports only itself
tasks.estimate_rationale: Module convention and the sibling core's layout are known; the work is defining types and boundary tests

complexity.justification: Designing types and protocols needs choices about what crosses the boundary, but the pattern exists in the sibling core

scope.justification: A new package with a handful of small modules and two test files, nothing wired to other code yet

duration.justification: The M1 core package was built the same way in one task of REQ-011; this one is smaller since there is no logic yet

risk.justification: The ports become the contract of every later task, so a wrong shape is expensive to change but nothing runs yet

coupling.justification: Later ledger and executor tasks consume these types and ports, so they need to agree on field names

confidence.justification: The module convention and the M1 contracts file were read; the sibling core is a direct precedent for layout and tests

acceptance_criteria: The package imports only the standard library and itself, verified by an AST test
Own request, receipt, status and event types round-trip through JSON and reject malformed input
The five ports are structural protocols that a plain test double can implement

tasks.title: SQLite WAL ledger: attempts keyed by unique attempt id and idempotency key, state machine, write-ahead event outbox, concurrent-writer safety
tasks.objective: A SQLite WAL ledger stores attempts and a write-ahead event outbox with unique keys and a checked state machine
tasks.estimate_rationale: Similar to the core's SQLite repository but with two unique keys and an outbox, not yet measured under contention

complexity.justification: Needs choices on schema, state machine and transaction boundaries, with durability and uniqueness subtleties

scope.justification: One storage file and its tests; the schema is small but every later task depends on it

duration.justification: The core's SQLite repository took comparable effort and this adds an outbox plus a second unique key

risk.justification: A wrong uniqueness or transition rule would allow two writers for one task, the central safety property of the executor

coupling.justification: T3 and the executor read and write the same tables, so the schema is a shared contract between them

confidence.justification: The core's SQLite repository was read and its pattern fits, but contention behaviour of the outbox is not yet measured

acceptance_criteria: A second insert with the same attempt id or idempotency key never creates a second row
Illegal attempt state transitions are refused and leave the stored row unchanged
Concurrent writers from threads and processes end with exactly one winner per key

tasks.title: Order validation and idempotent `start`/duplicate/conflict/`queue_full` semantics with persisted rejections before any side effect
tasks.objective: Orders are validated and persisted before any side effect, and replay, conflict and full queue answers are deterministic
tasks.estimate_rationale: Mostly rule logic over the ledger; the validation list is long but each rule is small

complexity.justification: Many validation rules and replay semantics must agree with how M1 retries and re-asks after a crash

scope.justification: Two small source files and a test file focused on the start path only

duration.justification: Comparable to the core's dispatch write-ahead tests, whose retry protocol was read for this estimate

risk.justification: Accepting a bad order or launching twice would put two writers on one task, which the whole design exists to prevent

coupling.justification: T2 supplies the ledger it writes to and T7 consumes the accepted records to run them

confidence.justification: The core's dispatch protocol was read so the replay rules match, but the executor side was never exercised yet

acceptance_criteria: The same idempotency key twice yields one record and a duplicate receipt
An unresolvable route or invalid model is rejected with a stable code and no side effect
A full queue returns a queue_full rejection that is persisted

tasks.title: `GitWorkspaces`: per-attempt worktree+branch from a resolved base, per-repository lock, durable journal, concurrency-safe allocation
tasks.objective: Every attempt gets its own worktree and branch from a resolved base under a per-repository lock with a journal
tasks.estimate_rationale: Git worktree races and crash points are subtle; the existing bt_worktree gives a precedent but not the lock design

complexity.justification: Concurrent git administration, lock choice and crash-recovery of half-made worktrees need design, not a known recipe

scope.justification: One focused module around git worktrees and its tests

duration.justification: bt_worktree allocation took shape in REQ-008 with similar crash handling; a per-repository lock is added here

risk.justification: A shared checkout or branch collision would corrupt another agent's work or the user's tree, hard to detect afterwards

coupling.justification: T5 snapshots the same worktrees and the executor allocates through this API, so semantics must be shared

confidence.justification: bt_worktree was read in full and already solves allocation journaling; the added locking is unproven under real races

acceptance_criteria: Parallel allocations on one repository produce distinct directories, branches and indexes
An unknown base ref is refused before any directory is created
A crash between journal write and git worktree add leaves a recoverable journal entry

tasks.title: Handoff snapshot: commits-only, dirty-only, both, empty, untracked, deleted, binary, spaces; snapshot commit under `refs/m3/`, binary patch, manifest, branch/index untouched, caps
tasks.objective: A handoff captures committed, uncommitted and untracked work in a private ref and patch without touching the attempt branch
tasks.estimate_rationale: Temporary-index plumbing and binary-safe diffs have many edge cases, each needing a real git test

complexity.justification: Git plumbing with a temporary index, binary diffs and caps has non-obvious failure modes that need experiments

evidence: spec:SPEC.md#US-4 (P1, Must) — Preserve the work, whatever happens
scope.justification: One module and a test file with a matrix of repository states

duration.justification: Writing each of eight scenarios with a real git repository is most of the time; the plumbing itself is short

evidence: spec:SPEC.md#US-4 (P1, Must) — Preserve the work, whatever happens
risk.justification: Losing or corrupting an agent's work is the exact failure this task prevents, and modifying the branch would break integration

coupling.justification: It operates on the worktrees that T4 allocates and shares their layout and journal

confidence.justification: The existing worktree candidate commit was read, but the temporary-index approach is new and not yet run against these cases

acceptance_criteria: Commits only, dirty only, both, empty, deleted, binary and space-in-path cases each yield a correct handoff
The attempt branch, its index and the base commit are identical before and after the snapshot
The patch applies cleanly on the base in a fresh worktree and reproduces the work

tasks.title: Detached shim: new session, timeout, capped head+tail output, atomic `shim.json`/`exit.json`, signal forwarding, process identity helpers
tasks.objective: A detached shim owns the agent process group, enforces timeout and caps and writes atomic exit and identity records
tasks.estimate_rationale: Process-group, signal and atomic-write behaviour are platform sensitive and need careful tests

complexity.justification: Signal forwarding, session leadership and start-time identity are subtle and OS specific

scope.justification: A standalone script plus helpers and tests, independent of the rest of the module

duration.justification: The driver already kills process groups on timeout; the shim adds atomic records, caps and identity

risk.justification: A shim that leaks processes or mislabels exits would break cancellation and restart reconciliation for every run

coupling.justification: The executor only calls the shim through its spec file and exit record, so interaction is narrow

confidence.justification: bt_driver's process-group handling was read and works in production, but the detached variant is new

acceptance_criteria: The shim writes shim.json at start and exit.json exactly once at the end
A timeout kills the whole process group including grandchildren and records reason timeout
Output beyond the cap is dropped with a counted byte total while the tail window is kept

tasks.title: `AgentExecutor` run loop: queue + bounded workers, prepare→allocate→spawn, watcher, started/heartbeat/finished/failed events with deterministic ids, outbox delivery and redelivery
tasks.objective: The executor queues, allocates, spawns and watches attempts and delivers started, heartbeat, finished and failed events idempotently
tasks.estimate_rationale: It integrates ledger, workspaces, shim and ports and carries most concurrency risk in the module

complexity.justification: Orchestrates threads, processes and durable state across three components with ordering and restart implications

scope.justification: The central class with the run loop and outbox delivery plus two test files; it is the largest single piece

duration.justification: The core's scheduler took the largest share of REQ-011; this executor is smaller but depends on three new parts

risk.justification: A flaw here can double-start work, lose events or deadlock the pool, affecting every attempt

coupling.justification: It joins ledger, workspace and shim and later classification, cancellation and reconciliation all extend this class

confidence.justification: The M1 dispatch design was read, but this class combines new components that have not run together yet

acceptance_criteria: A fake provider script runs to completion in its own worktree and produces started and finished events
Event ids are deterministic so redelivery of the outbox never duplicates a fact at the sink
The number of running attempts never exceeds the configured ceiling and extra orders wait in the queue
